newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank - expects to stay independent.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank - expects to stay independent.

text.p: Commerzbank AG said on Thursday it expected to be able to remain independent in future as its first-half results underlined the strength of its earnings.

"In view of the earnings strength expressed in these numbers, chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen expects that Commerzbank can continue down its successful path and shape its future alone," the bank said in its interim statement.
Earlier Commerzbank reported a 24.7 percent rise in group pre-tax profit to 1.65 billion marks in the first six months of 1997.

Commerzbank has been subject to renewed speculation that it faces takeover following Monday's news that two Bavarian banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, plan to merge.
The Bavarian merger will create Germany's second largest bank and relegate Commerzbank from third to fourth place in the league table.
Analaysts have said the merger has put added pressure on Commerzbank to find an ally, either at home or abroad.
